🅸🆂🆁🅰️🅴🅻 🅁🄴🄰🄻🅃🄸🄼🄴 - "Connecting the World to Israel in Realtime"

( VIDEO - a combined drone-fireworks show in China. Now consider if instead of civilian fireworks each drone was carrying and dropping an explosive charge. The capabilities of warfare are quickly changing. )

▪️EXPLOSIONS FROM LEBANON? Upper Galilee Regional Council: there are attacks on the Lebanon front as part of the IDF enforcement efforts. Sounds of explosions are heard in the Galilee area. (This was sent last night, unclear if still happening.)

🔪TERROR - JUDEA-SAMARIA - A Jewish shepherd from Gal Yosef farm was injured in the head by an armed terrorist with a pistol who fired 2 shots at him and apparently fled to the village of Al Mu'ayyer.

🔪TERROR - JERUSALEM - Last night in Jerusalem, a young Jewish man was stabbed after a group of youths shouted nationalist slogans at him and his friend. During the incident, one of the youths pulled out a knife and injured him. (It’s unclear from this report it is unclear whether this is Arab Jerusalem (legal) youths or other gang types.)

▪️HIGH COURT PETITION FOR THE RED CROSS - The Supreme Court judges held a discussion yesterday on the petition regarding Red Cross visits to the settlements. In response, Justice Minister Yariv Levin requested to organize a special screening of the Oct. 7 horror film for the judges.

▪️PRESIDENT PUSHES PLAN TO RETURN ‘PALESTINIAN’ WORKERS - renewed efforts are being made to bring back the Shin Bet initiative of returning ‘Palestinian’ workers to jobs, particularly construction, in Israel. The one pressing behind the scenes: President Herzog. "It is a big mistake not to bring in Palestinian workers when the Israeli economy is desperate for workers," Herzog said at a meeting with the Jerusalem Contractors Association last week. In the background: a shortage of at least 40,000 workers in the construction industry—and this is even before counting the needs for reconstruction following the campaign with Iran.

The concept: Israeli industry needs these low cost workers - with the construction industry not functioning at capacity due to a lack of workers, and people with jobs and an income have an investment in keeping things civil.

The reality: Many of the invaders on Oct. 7 were such workers, who had knowledge of areas being attacked because of their presence as workers, and in general ‘Palestinian’ society praised and supported the Oct. 7 invasion and massacre, and hostage taking, at over 75%. This is besides the trickle of terror attacks that occurred from such workers regularly, and flood of crime from such workers regularly.

As far as the lack of workers, Israel could easily import the workers from China, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, India etc if they want to. Instead the government bureaucracy has spent 2 years delaying and making the process as difficult as possible.

▪️HAREDI ANTI-DRAFT PROTESTS - nightly protests continue outside military prison #10, protesting the arrest of Haredi draft dodgers. Besides the original 2 that were sentenced to under-1-month sentences, an additional 3 haredi draft dodgers have been arrested.

.. Related: Blue & White party leader MK Gantz attacks the government over Haredi protests: "The fact that there are those who go out to violent protests against recruitment - while tens of thousands report for reserves and leave families at home - is shameful. But what is more shameful is a government that does nothing to actually recruit them.”

▪️ANTI-WAR PROTEST - Outside the Likud headquarters in Tel Aviv: The women's protest and families of (some) hostages in a demonstration - "Military pressure kills captives, only an agreement will save lives."

⭕THE GAZA AID RACKET - apparently there is a new aid mechanism called “Amjad Insurance - Aid Security” which Gazans can hire to take control of trucks and bring aid to them. These mechanisms charge fees for passage and "security" for every truck, with a significant Hamas tax.

♦️LEBANON - Lebanese sources report that the IDF carried out strikes in the Hosh area in the Tyre District of southern Lebanon overnight.

.. A multitude of secondary explosions as a result of another IDF strike in the area of the village Ansar in southern Lebanon. It appears that a Hezbollah weapons warehouse was hit in southern Lebanon.

.. The IDF says it struck several Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon overnight. The targets included weapon depots and a rocket launcher, according to the military.

.. Apparently also a targeted elimination in the Al-Bazouria area.

♦️GAZA - overnight air strikes in the northern Gaza Strip, per Arab reports.

🇸🇾SYRIA - civil conflict brewing? The “Coastal Shield Brigade” has threatened to "launch missiles and drones in the skies of occupied Damascus" if the illegally arrested Alawite Sheikh Saleh Mansour is not released within 48 hours.

IN PHOTOS | Philippine Army soldiers and their Australian counterparts are strengthening their interoperability through joint training under Exercise Amphibious Landing Operations (Exercise ALON) 2025, which runs from August 11 to 29 in Nueva Ecija.

Troops from the Army’s 84th Infantry “Victorious” Battalion of the 7th Infantry “Kaugnay” Division are participating in land warfare exercises at Fort Magsaysay and other training areas. Their training includes combat shooting, jungle operations, live-fire exercises, and urban combat supported by armor, artillery, and engineering units.

More than 3,600 personnel from the Philippines, Australia, the United States, and Canada are taking part in Exercise ALON, which also features amphibious landings, air-sea operations, and joint maneuvers. Japan, South Korea, New Zealand, and Indonesia are observing the exercises as part of broader regional defense cooperation. | via Rex Espiritu

For more info, visit https://t.co/rmQCnNSOvI.

IN PHOTOS | Ongoing flood-control works continue in Binondo, Manila, despite President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s recent disclosure of anomalies in several projects. 

Mayor Isko Moreno reminded the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) and the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) on Thursday (August 21) to secure permits from the city government before undertaking such infrastructure works, stressing that all projects must align with Manila’s City Drainage Master Plan to prevent flooding and ensure accountability.

📷 Norman Cruz

For more info, visit https://t.co/rmQCnNSOvI.
